Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

what?! interjection

surprise, or not having caught it

also huh?, eh?, what did you say?, pardon?, come again?

classical

Ter. Ad. 700: Quid? jam uxōrem?

Quid?

what?

Alone, it asks for more or protests; followed by the word that surprised (Quid? jam uxōrem?).

Other words

  • Hem? — huh? eh?

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 696

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    The startled “huh?” of comedy (Lewis & Short: surprise).

  • Quid ais? — what are you saying? what?

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.13.3: quid ais? Caesarem nunc dēfendit Cūriō?; Plaut. Amph. 364b

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    Of surprise or disbelief at what was said; also simply “tell me”. For the disbelieving “really?”, ain’? (see really?).

Examples

  • Quid? jam uxōrem? — Jam. — Jam? — Jam, quantum potest.

    What? a wife now? — Now. — Now?! — Now, as fast as can be.Ter. Ad. 700

  • Bonō animō es: dūcēs uxōrem hanc. — Hem. — Bonō animō es, inquam.

    Cheer up: you’ll marry her. — Huh? — Cheer up, I said.Ter. Ad. 696

  • quid ais? Caesarem nunc dēfendit Cūriō?

    What? Curio is now defending Caesar?Cic. Fam. 2.13.3

  • vocō, quaerō ecquid litterārum. negant. quid ais? inquam, nihilne ā Pompōniō?

    I call them, ask if there are any letters. They say no. “What?” I say, “nothing from Pomponius?”Cic. Att. 2.8.1

See also what, really?, oh!.
